## Final answers

**Q1 — Most earnings per square foot of shelf:** **no record.** The database has no shelf-area/space fields at all (only `dc_slot` codes, pack sizes, price and cost), so revenue or margin per square foot of shelf cannot be computed for any product. (June revenue per SKU was computed as a sanity check, but it is not a per-sq-ft measure.)

**Q2 — June 2026 write-off lines with reason 'expired':** **19 lines** (489 units). The other 15 June write-off lines were 'damaged' (15 units).

**Q3 — Failed UPI payment on a customer's bank statement:** The bank statement showed the amount **debited/charged even though the till recorded the UPI as failed**; the PSP report shows the transaction status as **'returned'**, and the complaint resolution states **"customer's bank returned the money"** (i.e., the debit was reversed/credited back). Three such cases in June 2026: ₹73.65 (3 Jun), ₹378.31 (10 Jun), ₹215.34 (25 Jun) — in each case the till showed "failed: no response" and the shopper paid cash instead.

**Q4 — Why shoppers choose cash, card or UPI:** **no record.** The records show only *which* tender was used (June approved: UPI 18,384, cash 7,829, card 3,864; UPI also had 589 declined, 145 failed, 48 "failed: no response"), but there is no table, column, note or survey capturing shoppers' reasons/motivation for choosing a tender.

**Q5 — Markdown for expiring milk:** **no record.** There is no markdown/pricing-policy table or column (no discount, markdown or policy fields exist). The database only holds use-by dates (`fresh_deliveries.use_by`), forecasts and expired write-offs, so the required markdown percentage cannot be read from records.

**Q6 — Brands vs private label:** **no record.** `store.products` has no brand or private-label flag; all 11 SKUs carry generic names (e.g. "Whole wheat atta 5 kg", "Full cream milk 500 ml pouch") with no manufacturer/brand attribute, so brand vs private-label preference cannot be measured.

**Q7 — Stock stolen vs counted wrong:** **no record for theft.** No record in June 2026 is classified as stolen/shrinkage. The only discrepancies recorded are counting/picking errors: scheduled full counts (22 lines, net −55 units; 120 units short, 65 over), manager-requested counts (3 lines, net +93 units), and warehouse adjustments "short pick: slot count variance" (−160 units ATTA-WW-1KG) and "cycle count variance" (+64 units ATTA-WW-5KG). So nothing is attributed to theft.

**Q8 — Does the 5 kg atta pack sell at the expense of the 1 kg pack?** **Yes — the records point that way.** POS units: 5 kg fell from 631 (May) to 567 (June) while 1 kg rose from 743 to 826; the 5 kg pack was audited "empty" on 12 and 26 June (1 kg always on shelf); the 26 June count found 5 kg book 63 / counted 0 while 1 kg book 106 / counted 263 (+157); warehouse adjustments show 1 kg short by 160 units and 5 kg over by 64 units. This pattern is consistent with 5 kg stock being sold but recorded as 1 kg units (cannibalisation/mis-scan), though no explicit mis-scan record exists.

SELECT * FROM store.write_offs ORDER BY date, sku;

SELECT extract(hour from bill_ts)::int hr,
       count(distinct bill_id) bills,
       count(*) lines,
       round(count(distinct bill_id)::numeric / count(distinct bill_ts::date),1) bills_per_day
FROM store.pos_lines
WHERE bill_ts >= '2026-06-01' AND bill_ts < '2026-07-01'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

SELECT status, count(*) n, count(distinct bill_ref) bills, sum(amount_inr) amt
FROM payments.psp_upi_report GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC;
SELECT * FROM payments.psp_upi_report LIMIT 10;

SELECT status, count(*) n, count(distinct sku) skus, min(audit_ts)::text mn, max(audit_ts)::text mx
FROM store.shelf_audits GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC;
SELECT * FROM store.shelf_audits ORDER BY audit_ts LIMIT 20;

SELECT bill_id, count(*) attempts, count(*) FILTER (WHERE till_status='approved') approved,
       string_agg(till_status||'@'||ts::text, ' | ' ORDER BY ts) detail
FROM payments.pos_payments
GROUP BY bill_id
HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE till_status='approved')=0
ORDER BY min(ts) LIMIT 20;

SELECT bill_id, count(*) attempts, count(*) FILTER (WHERE till_status='approved') approved,
       string_agg(till_status||'@'||ts::text, ' | ' ORDER BY ts) detail
FROM payments.pos_payments
WHERE ts>='2026-06-01' AND ts<'2026-07-01'
GROUP BY bill_id
HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE till_status='approved')=0
ORDER BY min(ts) LIMIT 20;
